item.text: {"question_id":"5B.1","answer":"The evidence supports a mixed, partially broad-based but not clearly sustainable prosperity agenda under López Obrador, with strong attribution for the administration’s formal priorities and major policy choices but weaker attribution for aggregate outcomes. Favorable evidence includes constitutional and legislative commitments to social rights, direct transfers, employment, and inequality reduction; a 20% 2023 minimum-wage increase; and expanded social-program budgets (BATCH-0030-E007; BATCH-0031-E008; BATCH-0049-E006). Implementation and outcome evidence is mixed: labor poverty fell from 40.1% to 37.3% and real per-capita labor income rose 11.3% between the third quarters of 2022 and 2023, while 2023 GDP growth, employment, and inflation performance were favorable, although nearshoring, U.S. recovery, remittances, monetary policy, and other external or institutional factors also contributed (BATCH-0054-E002; BATCH-0016-E013; BATCH-0052-E019). The contrary evidence is material. Universal transfers shifted a smaller share of social spending toward the poorest, and the universal pension’s fiscal sustainability was questioned; CONEVAL found poverty reduction alongside nearly unchanged extreme poverty, sharply increased health-service deprivation, and persistent social deprivation (BATCH-0012-E016; BATCH-0032-E002; BATCH-0032-E003). The 2023 priority-program budget placed 52% in the older-adult pension category, while a health program representing about 13% lacked a clearly identified target population; four priority programs representing almost 20% of the budget were classified as management programs that did not measure results, and monitoring recommendations had been disregarded to varying degrees (BATCH-0052-E003; BATCH-0052-E004). Fiscal and investment choices also weakened the sustainability case: substantial PEMEX support continued despite losses and weak finances; the IMF criticized the proposed 2024 budget as procyclical and called for better-targeted social protection, more productive and efficient spending, and stronger fiscal transparency; and energy policy created uncertainty by replacing auctions with nonmarket-based arrangements (BATCH-0014-E014; BATCH-0016-E015; BATCH-0017-E006). Finally, health investment was repeatedly under-executed while flagship projects received greater resources, and the Maya Train opened partially in 2023 amid delays, large cost increases, incomplete construction, uncertain costs, and limited evidence of feasibility or broad local utility (BATCH-0048-E010; BATCH-0030-E004). Thus, the record shows genuine broad-welfare objectives and some favorable household and macroeconomic results, but also untargeted or politically salient allocations, weak monitoring and implementation, exclusionary or adverse distributional effects, and unresolved fiscal and productivity risks. The evidence does not establish that the agenda was principally loyalty purchasing or short-term popularity, but it also does not support treating formal objectives, appropriations, or 2023 outcomes as proof of broad-based sustainable prosperity.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0049-E006","BATCH-0054-E002","BATCH-0016-E013","BATCH-0052-E019"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0016-E015","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0048-E010","BATCH-0030-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence mixes 2023 policies and outcomes with 2018–2022 results and projections for 2024; it does not provide a complete 2023 executed-budget incidence study.","Budget allocations and formal objectives do not establish service quality, broad incidence, or sustainable welfare effects.","National GDP, poverty, employment, and inflation outcomes cannot be assigned solely to López Obrador because of monetary policy, pandemic recovery, nearshoring, U.S. demand, remittances, subnational action, and other external factors.","Some adverse findings concern projected fiscal risks, incomplete projects, or earlier implementation periods rather than fully observed 2023 results.","Evidence of political popularity or loyalty effects is suggestive in the universal-transfer discussion but does not prove that loyalty purchasing was the administration’s dominant motive."] ,"corrections_made":["Reduced the favorable weight assigned to stated objectives, approved budgets, and the minimum-wage decision by separating policy intent from execution and independently evaluated results.","Added the omitted 2023 evidence that the older-adult pension category accounted for 52% of priority-program spending, four management programs represented almost 20% of the priority budget and did not measure results, and monitoring recommendations were disregarded to varying degrees.","Removed the unsupported implication that BATCH-0052-E019 independently established a broad-based sustainable prosperity agenda; it is used only for mixed 2023 outcomes, attribution limits, and fiscal-risk context.","Qualified the IMF evidence so that country-level macroeconomic performance is not treated as personal causal proof for López Obrador.","Preserved uncertainty around the period, attribution, execution, distribution, and causal interpretation."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full 2023 executed-budget and household-incidence assessment could materially clarify whether formal allocations produced broad rather than politically concentrated benefits.","Independent audits and outcome evaluations of priority programs, PEMEX support, flagship projects, and health investment could change the implementation and sustainability assessment.","More direct evidence is needed to distinguish policy effectiveness from electoral or loyalty-purchasing motives."]}
